evals.query: In my Kora service (Java), add a job that logs a heartbeat every 30 seconds with an initial delay of 10 seconds, using the built-in JVM scheduler.
expected_behavior: Uses @ScheduleAtFixedRate(initialDelay = 10, period = 30, unit = ChronoUnit.SECONDS) imported from io.koraframework.scheduling.jdk.annotation
Marks the enclosing class @Component from io.koraframework.common.annotation and gives the method no arguments

Adds io.koraframework:scheduling-jdk (version from the io.koraframework:kora-bom BOM) plus annotationProcessor "io.koraframework:annotation-processors", and extends SchedulingJdkModule on the @KoraApp interface
Does not use ru.tinkoff.kora packages, the kora-parent BOM, a Spring @Scheduled annotation, or an external scheduler library

evals.query: I added @ScheduleWithFixedDelay to a method on a Kotlin @Component class in my Kora 2 service and someone told me the class has to be `open` or the job silently never runs. Is that right?
expected_behavior: Says No: the scheduling processor generates a $<Class>_SchedulingModule that calls the component through ValueOf<T>, so no AOP proxy is created and the class does not need to be open (Kotlin) or non-final (Java)
Notes that the migrated Kora 2.0 examples ship a plain `@Component class` in Kotlin and `@Component public final class` in Java and both schedule correctly
Explains that `open` is required only when a proxy-based aspect such as @Log, @Retryable, @Timeout or @Cacheable is added to the same class
Points at the real reasons a job never fires: the class is not in the graph (missing @Component), the method takes arguments, is private, or is suspend
Does not repeat the Kora 1.x claim that a non-open class silently skips schedule generation

evals.query: My Kotlin Kora job needs to call two suspend repository functions in parallel, so I marked the scheduled function `suspend fun refreshCaches()`. It won't build. What now?
expected_behavior: States that a suspend function is not a valid scheduled contract and KSP fails the build with "Suspend methods are not supported by the scheduling generator"
Explains that Kora 2.0 contracts are synchronous and run on virtual threads, so the repository/client calls become plain blocking calls
Removes `suspend` and, for real parallelism, points at java.util.concurrent.StructuredTaskScope with --enable-preview rather than reintroducing coroutines
Does not suggest runBlocking inside the scheduled method as the recommended design, and does not use Mono/Flux or CompletionStage as a Kora contract

evals.query: Kotlin Kora 2 project: which KSP artifact do I need so @ScheduleAtFixedRate actually generates something? I found ru.tinkoff.kora:scheduling-ksp on Maven Central.
expected_behavior: Rejects scheduling-ksp: it is a Kora 1.x leftover on Maven Central and is not constrained by the 2.0.0.RC1 kora-bom
Gives ksp("io.koraframework:symbol-processors") as the normal aggregate, noting the module-specific artifact is io.koraframework:scheduling-symbol-processor
Keeps the version coming from platform("io.koraframework:kora-bom:...") rather than pinning the artifact
Adds implementation("io.koraframework:scheduling-jdk") and the SchedulingJdkModule on @KoraApp

evals.query: Porting a Kora 1.x service to 2.0. My application.conf has scheduling { threads = 10, shutdownWait = "60s" } and the app starts fine, but neither setting seems to do anything. Why?
expected_behavior: Explains that both are Kora 1.x keys and unknown HOCON keys are ignored without any warning, which is why the app starts green
States that scheduling.shutdownWait moved to scheduling.jdk.shutdownWait (SchedulingJdkModule reads the config at path scheduling.jdk)
States that scheduling.threads was removed with no replacement key: the ScheduledThreadPoolExecutor core size is the number of jobs declared with config = "..."
Warns that with zero config-driven jobs the pool runs on a single thread, so annotation-only jobs serialize behind each other
Does not invent a replacement thread-count key or claim the 1.x keys still work

evals.query: I want a Grafana panel for how long my Kora scheduled jobs take. I added the metrics module but scheduling_job_duration never appears. Java project.
expected_behavior: Identifies that scheduling.telemetry.metrics.enabled defaults to false in Kora 2.0 and must be set to true explicitly
Shows the config, e.g. scheduling.telemetry.metrics.enabled = true, and notes a MeterRegistry component must also be in the graph

Names the meter scheduling.job.duration (a Micrometer Timer) and its tags code.function.name, system.name.simple, system.name.canonical, error.type, plus the system.config tag carrying the config path for jobs that declare one
Mentions that logging.enabled also defaults to false while tracing.enabled defaults to true, and that per-job overrides live under <job-config-path>.telemetry
Does not claim metrics are on by default or reference a scheduling.metrics.* key outside telemetry

evals.query: My Kora job with @ScheduleAtFixedRate(period = 60, unit = ChronoUnit.SECONDS) sometimes takes 90 seconds. Will two copies run at the same time, and should I add a synchronized block?
expected_behavior: Says no: @ScheduleAtFixedRate delegates to ScheduledExecutorService.scheduleAtFixedRate, whose contract is that a late execution starts late but never runs concurrently, and Kora additionally wraps every run of a job in a per-job ReentrantLock
Explains the real difference: fixed rate measures start-to-start and tries to keep cadence, fixed delay measures end-to-start and always leaves an idle gap
Rejects the synchronized block as unnecessary for the same job, while noting different jobs can run concurrently subject to the pool
If pool sizing comes up, says the core size is the number of jobs declared with config = "..." and that there is no scheduling.threads key in 2.0
Does not repeat the Kora 1.x claim that @ScheduleAtFixedRate allows overlapping executions

evals.query: I need one job in my Kora 2 service to run at 03:00 every day. Single instance, nothing to persist. Do I have to pull in Quartz?
expected_behavior: Says no: Kora 2.0 ships @ScheduleWithCron in io.koraframework.scheduling.jdk.annotation, backed by the in-process CronExpression evaluator in scheduling-jdk
Shows @ScheduleWithCron("0 0 3 * * ?") on a no-argument method of a @Component, with 5, 6 or 7 space-separated fields
Notes the expression is parsed during graph build so a bad expression fails startup with IllegalArgumentException, and that it fires in the JVM default time zone
Notes the Quartz-only modifiers L, W, # and C are not supported by the JDK evaluator
Does not add the scheduling-quartz artifact or QuartzModule for this requirement

evals.query: We run four replicas of a Kora service and a nightly reconciliation job must execute exactly once across the cluster and survive restarts. Can the JDK scheduler do that?
expected_behavior: Says no: scheduling-jdk holds no state, so every replica runs every job and nothing survives the process
Routes to the kora-aop-scheduling-quartz skill for a persistent JDBC job store, clustering and misfire handling

Distinguishes clearly: plain in-process cron is fine on the JDK scheduler via @ScheduleWithCron, but persistence, clustering, @ScheduleWithTrigger, @DisallowConcurrentExecution and Quartz-only cron modifiers are the Quartz module's job
Does not invent a cluster or persistence option on the JDK annotations

evals.query: My Kora 2 batch import job processes a long list and blocks shutdown for minutes. I already check Thread.currentThread().isInterrupted() in the loop but it never triggers. What is going on?
expected_behavior: Explains that Kora 2.0 never interrupts a running scheduled job: the job's release() blocks on the same lock the run holds until the method returns, and it cancels the schedule with cancel(false), which does not interrupt
Explains that scheduling.jdk.shutdownWait is the executor's awaitTermination budget after the jobs are already stopped, so it does not bound a running job
Recommends cooperative cancellation instead: a bounded batch per run, an in-run deadline, and timeouts on every blocking call, keeping the work unit well under the container kill timeout
Keeps interrupt handling only where the code genuinely blocks on something interruptible, rather than as the shutdown mechanism
Does not tell the user to raise scheduling.shutdownWait (a 1.x key) or claim SIGTERM interrupts the job

evals.query: Kotlin Kora 2 service: I need a data sync task that waits 2 minutes after each run finishes before running again, and the timing must come from config, not from the code.
expected_behavior: Uses @ScheduleWithFixedDelay so the gap is measured after completion, on a no-argument member function of a @Component class
Sets config = "scheduling.jobs.sync" (or another path that does not collide with scheduling.jdk or scheduling.telemetry) and defines initialDelay and delay under it as HOCON/YAML durations
Explains that annotation attributes become defaults of the generated config interface and config values win, and that omitting `delay` from the annotation makes the config key mandatory
Mentions that the per-job path also accepts a telemetry block overriding scheduling.telemetry for that job
Does not use a `unit` key in the config file or reach for Quartz cron for a fixed-delay requirement

evals.query: What Gradle dependencies and processors do I need to make @ScheduleAtFixedRate work in a Java Kora 2 project?
expected_behavior: Adds platform("io.koraframework:kora-bom:$koraVersion") with koraVersion=2.0.0.RC1 from mavenCentral(), and io.koraframework:scheduling-jdk with no explicit version
Includes annotationProcessor "io.koraframework:annotation-processors" (Kotlin: ksp("io.koraframework:symbol-processors")) and explains that without it no job component is generated
Extends SchedulingJdkModule on the @KoraApp interface and adds a config module such as HoconConfigModule
Mentions the Java 25 toolchain requirement for Kora 2.0 artifacts
Does not use ru.tinkoff.kora:kora-parent, does not pin individual io.koraframework artifact versions, and does not omit the processor
